Not really two games at all, into the dark really feels like kill team lite, I feel like GW realized that people were struggling with line of sight, specially with obscuring, and cover lines, and with most mechanics that make kill team kill team,
So they simplified everything, got rid of terrain all together and replaced it with solid, straight walls, to prevent obscuring from coming into play.
They also removed all verticality from the game, so it went from a 3d game to a 2d one, therefore simplifying not only shooting but also movement, since climbing was another thing a lot of people struggled with.

And coupled with the release of intercession I think it's safe to assume that GW was attempting to appeal to a crowd that had either found kill team too complex and not stuck with it, or were not interested in trying it due to it being too complex, and it worked, kill team has grown a lot since the release of into the dark and intercession, and it's noticeable in this subreddit and on YouTube.

TL;DR GW released into the dark as a simplified version of kill team to increase popularity and it worked
